summary: Configured node1, node2, and node3 as a three-member MariaDB 10.11 / Galera 26.4 multi-master cluster on Ubuntu 24.04. Verified writes on any member replicate to the others, confirmed continued availability and writes with one member stopped, confirmed automatic resync (IST) when the stopped member returned, and completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes with proven boot-identity change and full post-restart cluster/data recovery.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-client, galera-4, rsync on node1, node2, node3 from Ubuntu universe repos
Added CLUSTER_HOSTS entries to /etc/hosts on all three nodes
Wrote /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/60-galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_provider, wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3, per-node wsrep_node_address/name, wsrep_sst_method=rsync
Bootstrapped cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster, then joined node2 and node3 via systemctl start mariadb
Enabled mariadb service on boot on all three nodes
Generated an appuser DB credential on node1 with openssl rand, created via CREATE USER (replicated cluster-wide by Galera), stored only in root-owned file, never printed
Created galeratest.t table and performed cross-node write/read tests confirming multi-master replication
Stopped mariadb on node2 to simulate an outage, verified 2-node quorum (Primary/Synced) and continued writes/reads on node1 and node3
Restarted mariadb on node2, verified automatic IST resync back to cluster size 3 with all data present including writes made while it was down
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster/data health baseline on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 one at a time preserving quorum on the other two, polling until each came back and confirming boot_id changed
Verified post-restart on each node: mariadb active, wsrep_cluster_size=3, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, and galeratest.t row count intact

evidence.requirement: Three-member Galera cluster formed, all nodes Primary/Synced
evidence.summary: node1 bootstraps as size 1; node2 joins making size 2; node3 joins making size 3, all Primary/Synced

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member available on other members
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 visible on node2 and node3; row inserted on node2 visible on node3; row inserted on node3 visible back on node1 — full mesh replication confirmed

evidence.requirement: Database stays available when one member is down
evidence.summary: node2 stopped; node1 shows cluster size 2/Primary/Synced and accepts a write; node3 accepts a write and sees node1's write, proving continued availability with quorum of 2

evidence.requirement: Automatic resynchronization of a returning member
evidence.summary: node2 restarted after being down; cluster size returns to 3/Primary/Synced and node2's local table already contains the rows written by node1 and node3 while it was offline (automatic IST)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4d70780a.../cluster healthy; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; new boot_id ef456c56...; post-restart cluster size 3/Primary/Synced with intact data

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 37344ae4.../cluster healthy; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id f9c6e6e6...; post-restart cluster size 3/Primary/Synced with intact data

evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id df9e2dce.../cluster healthy; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id e6ae2e16...; post-restart cluster size 3/Primary/Synced with intact data

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health and data consistency after all restarts
evidence.summary: node1 shows cluster size 3, Primary, Synced, and all 5 rows present after all three nodes have been sequentially restarted
